tagline.text: A small craft town in inland Bohol with a Sunday basket market and Mag-aso Falls

location.label: Location
location.text: Poblacion, Antequera, Bohol (about 19 km north of Tagbilaran)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May dry season (year-round for the Sunday market)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: Published fare from Tagbilaran ₱25. Basket-weaving eco-tour ₱400 plus transport

children.text: Antequera is a Bohol basket-making town north of Tagbilaran. Browse finished wares at the Sunday morning market, or book a weekday visit to a weaver’s home three days ahead. Check access to Mag-Aso Falls before traveling.
Antequera is a municipality of about
118 km²
in the northwest interior of Bohol, roughly
19 km

north of the provincial capital, Tagbilaran. It borders Calape, San Isidro, Balilihan, Cortes, Maribojoc and Loon, and its elevation ranges from 3 m on the coastal side to 322 m in the hills. According to the 2024 census it has about 14,900 residents (14,990 in 2020) spread over 21 barangays, a quiet farming community. There are no beaches or large resorts here; the appeal is a close look at how ordinary Boholanos live.

Antequera is known as Bohol's basket-weaving center. Many villagers make a living weaving baskets, trays, mats and table accessories from bamboo, rattan and nito (a vine fiber), and carpentry and bamboo and wood furniture are major cottage industries too. Farming centers on coconut, rice, corn and root crops. The basket market held on Sunday mornings is the day when everything the town makes, from big pieces to small ones, comes together in one place, so the first rule of visiting Antequera is to plan it for a Sunday.
Antequera was formerly Agad, a barangay of Maribojoc, and became a separate municipality on
March 17, 1876
. One account traces its name to a person from Antequera in Spain. Choose the Sunday market or weekday weaving tour according to your visit date, and check access before adding the falls.

A word on what to expect. Antequera is not a polished tourist site; it is a place where everyday life goes on and visitors stop by for a while. Signage and facilities are sparse, and part of the fun is asking locals for directions and bargaining as you go. It is a small 4th-class municipality whose residents live mostly on farming and handicrafts, so the daily life of the artisans stands out more than tourism does. Ask the weavers' permission before taking photos, and if you buy something and chat a little, they will often tell you how it is made and what materials it uses.
It is held early on Sunday morning at the town gym, next to the municipal compound. Artisans bring baskets, mats, trays and decorations they made themselves, and by about

at the latest a lot of the stock is gone. If you miss market day, the tourism office also displays crafts. Baskets come in many sizes and weaves, so it helps to decide on a use first, such as a fruit basket, a laundry basket or a decorative tray, before you choose.
According to the
municipal tour page

, visitors meet at the Tourism Information and Display Center in the municipal compound in Poblacion before visiting a weaver’s home. Published hours are weekdays, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., for ages 10 and up, with three days’ advance booking.
This forest waterfall changed after the 2013 earthquake and 2014 flooding. Ask the municipal tourism desk about trail access and permission to swim on the day of your visit.

The Antequera tourism information office is a small air-conditioned room inside the municipal compound. Even on days other than market day you can see woven goods and get an introduction to the town, which makes it a good first stop.

Besides baskets, there are workshops making bamboo and wood furniture all over town. You can look at roadside workshops as you drive past; large pieces are hard to buy because of their bulk, but watching them being made is worth seeing. The carpentry skills of local artisans are also used to build houses, which makes the trade one pillar of the local economy.
The feast of the town's patron, Our Lady of the Holy Rosary, with Mass and a village celebration, is said to take place every year in
October (the last Saturday or the third Sunday, depending on the source; confirm locally)
, and the feast of the second patron, St. Anthony of Padua, is said to fall on
June 13
. On feast days the town is lively, with food and processions to see.

blocks.title: A drive through the Bohol countryside

children.text: Unlike the coastal highway, this is an inland road that winds between rice fields and coconut palms, and it is a pleasure to drive slowly in a rental car or with a driver. The town borders neighboring municipalities, so it is easy to head on toward the Chocolate Hills.
Set out from your hotel in Tagbilaran or Panglao. From Tagbilaran it is about
30 minutes
by car.
Browse the artisans' goods at the basket market in front of the town gym. Most prices can be bargained.
After the market, take a break at a nearby shop. Book the weaving tour separately for a weekday.
Visit Mag-Aso Falls if access is allowed. Continue to the next stop if the falls are closed.
Return to Tagbilaran for lunch, or continue toward Loboc.
Choose the market on Sunday or a prebooked basket-weaving tour on a weekday.
Rent a vehicle and drive to Antequera.
Visit the market on Sunday, or join a prebooked basket-weaving tour on a weekday.
Drive on along inland roads and have lunch.
Add one more inland sight, such as a Loboc River cruise or the Tarsier Sanctuary.
There are direct flights from Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG). Airlines and schedules change by season, so check when you book.
You can also route through Cebu. High-speed ferries run from Cebu to Tagbilaran, and from the port you continue to Antequera by road.
Flight routes and ferry schedules change often, so check the latest announcements.
By car or rental car it is about
, usually around
30 minutes
The
municipality’s transport directions
list Antequera buses or jeepneys from Cogon Market or Dao Terminal in Tagbilaran. The published fare is ₱25. Check departures and the return service before boarding.
Within town and out to the falls, use a tricycle or a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal). Negotiate the fare or agree on a charter price.
Ask the municipal tourism desk whether the access road and parking are usable before heading to the falls.
The basket market is on Sunday morning and the booked weaving tour runs on weekdays. Check trail access and currents at the falls even during the
December–May
dry season.

In the rainy season the water at the falls can swell and run strong, and the paths get slippery after rain. Records say floods from a tropical storm in 2014 changed the falls, so avoid swimming after heavy rain.

. The waterfall fee is a historical example.

There are not many large lodgings in Antequera itself, so most visitors come from hotels in Tagbilaran or Panglao. It is about 30 minutes by car from Tagbilaran, so lodging is no obstacle. To catch the Sunday morning market you need an early start, so it helps to stay in Tagbilaran the night before.

The town has small eateries and corner stores (sari-sari stores) where you can get simple meals and drinks. For a proper meal you will have more choice if you go back to Tagbilaran or eat along the way toward Loboc. The food is Bohol home cooking built around rice, fish and coconut dishes.

On market morning, grab a coconut drink or a simple bread at a local shop, then have lunch after the falls; that order feels natural. If you cannot find a restaurant, asking your driver for a nearby place is the quickest way. Carry water and snacks in the midday heat.
Arrive early on Sunday (before
) to see the widest variety of baskets.
Baskets are bulky and hard to carry on as cabin luggage. Small trays, mats and decorations are easier to travel with.
Bargain down from the asking price, but these are things artisans spent time making, so it is polite not to push too hard.
Bring swimwear, a change of clothes, a waterproof bag and water shoes for the falls.
Bring plenty of cash. Cards are hard to use at the market and the falls.
Book with the municipal tourism desk at least three days ahead and confirm the meeting time and transport cost.
If you drive, do not leave things in the car at the falls parking lot, and keep valuables with you.
Before going to the basket market, confirm the market time once more with your hotel staff to avoid a wasted trip.
Before you buy a craft item, check it for mold or insect traces, and check the import rules of your home country for plant-based products.
Check access and safety rules for Mag-Aso Falls with the tourism desk first. Stay out of the gorge when entry is restricted or rain causes high water.
The stairs and rocks down to the falls are slippery after rain.
After swimming it is easy to get into the car wet, so bring a towel and a change of clothes.
There is no market except on Sunday, so check the day of the week.
Fees and hours can change, so check the latest information locally.
If you bring children, let them swim only in shallow areas and keep an adult beside them at all times.
Mobile signal is weak in places on the inland roads, so download your map in advance.
A waterfall a short drive from town, where you can walk down forest stairs for about
10 minutes
and enjoy a swim.
Bohol's provincial capital, about
30 minutes
by car from Antequera, with restaurants and shopping in the city center.
A classic river cruise on the inland route, famous for its lunch buffet cruises.
A place to see the tarsier, Bohol's mascot, and easy to combine with an inland itinerary in the same direction as Antequera.
